newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Nomura rates Hungary's Pick salami-maker as buy.
newsitem.headline: Nomura rates Hungary's Pick salami-maker as buy.

text.p: Hungarian meat processor Pick can expect to benefit from a revival of domestic consumer spending over the next two years, an analyst report said, rating the shares as a "buy".

"We expect Pick's domestic sales to recover over the coming two years," Martin Gollner, a Nomura analyst said. "With earnings forecast to increase by around 27 percent next year, the stock looks attractively valued on an estimated 1997 p/e ratio of 5."
The report, by Nomura Equity Research, added that lower costs and increased domestic sales will ensure the company meets its 1996 targets.

With a 20 percent increase in first half pre-tax profits and a 23 percent rise in first half sales, Gollner said he expects the company to meet its full-year forecasts of 21 percent higher sales of 28.5 billion forints and 22 percent higher pre-tax profits of 2.3 billion forints.

Although deliveries to central Europe and Russia still offer "good opportunities" over the medium to long term, exports may grow only slowly as Germany, the group's main export market, seems to be close to saturation, the report said.
Costs, however, will be lower this year as pig prices fell in the first half after rising 40 percent in 1995.
"Although pig prices are on the rise again, we believe that the average increase should be not more than 10 percent this year," Gollner predicted.

A turnaround this year in domestic sales, which has seen an 11 percent increase so far this year after a 9 percent fall in 1995, should be followed by even stronger growth next year, supported by a recovery in Hungarian spending which Nomura predicts will come in the second half of 1997.
